stories.title: Cloudflare Implements Cache Transcoding to Optimize Cache Storage with Zstandard
stories.snippet: Cloudflare employs Cache Transcoding, compressing text assets like HTML and CSS with Zstandard before caching them. This method significantly reduces storage and costs by accepting a small, repeated decode cost for frequently read cached data.
stories.summary: Cloudflare implemented Cache Transcoding to optimize cache storage by compressing response bodies with Zstandard before writing them to disk. The data remains compressed throughout its time in the cache and during transfers between data centers, only being decoded just before reaching the client. To avoid wasting CPU cycles, they skip recompressing content that is already compressed, such as images and videos, and instead focus on text-based assets including HTML, CSS, JSON, and JavaScript. Using zstd level 3, this approach achieves a 2.8x reduction in storage. The tradeoff is favorable because cached assets are read far more often than they are written, making the small recurring decode cost worthwhile compared to the one-time compression effort.

stories.title: Choose a Depth, Not a Duration, To Navigate Rabbit Holes
stories.snippet: I think it is a good thing when you find almost everything interesting. Curiosity that keeps pulling you deeper into a topic is not a bug, but a feature.
stories.summary: Arpit Bhayani argues that curiosity-driven rabbit holes are valuable, but the real problem is not knowing when to stop exploring them. While most people rely on timeboxing to limit their exploration, the author prefers a different approach: choosing a depth rather than a duration. At a predetermined point, he treats whatever lies below as a fair assumption or black box and moves on. This method works because rabbit holes are not flat—the first few layers are usually directly relevant, but past a certain depth, you are learning about the implementation of the implementation, which rarely changes how the layer above it is used. Ultimately, timeboxing optimizes for how much time you spend, while "depth-boxing" optimizes for understanding what matters.

stories.title: Design Multi-Context Processing Tools as Capabilities, Not Endpoints
stories.snippet: One anti-pattern I keep seeing: mapping MCP tools 1:1 onto a REST API.
stories.summary: A common anti-pattern when designing MCP tools is mapping them 1:1 onto REST API endpoints, with a typical user API requiring createUser, updateUser, getUser, listUsers, deleteUser, getUserPermissions, and setUserPermissions functions. This approach loads seven entries into the model's context window on every request, consuming context and increasing costs over time. The recommended approach treats each tool as a capability rather than an endpoint, consolidating multiple operations such as creation, updates, and permissions into a single tool like manage_user that returns a clean summary. Since most MCP clients load all registered tool schemas into context before processing prompts, keeping the tool surface small matters. The MCP server should function as a service layer in front of the API rather than a pass-through proxy, letting the API stay granular while the MCP layer controls what the model actually sees.

stories.title: How to protect yourself from workslop
stories.summary: Workslop refers to AI-generated text sent by colleagues or bosses that creates an asymmetrical effort problem, since producing it takes almost no effort but reading it still does. The easiest solution is to tell people to stop, though this only works if you have enough authority or social capital. When that's not possible, you can treat the sender like a high-latency interface to a coding agent by giving them step-by-step instructions. Another approach is using AI to fight AI, either by asking an LLM to extract the salient points or to generate an entire response. Biasing toward calls or in-person meetings forces effort symmetry and prevents AI content from being pasted at you. Finally, you can simply match the sender's lack of effort by skimming, deferring, or ignoring workslop, especially for long status updates from outside your organization.

stories.title: You have to beat the models at something
stories.summary: Engineers increasingly need to demonstrate value over replacement: what they can contribute that models such as GPT-5.6-Sol or Claude Opus 5 cannot. Coding agents are improving at working on large codebases, so retreating to technically difficult engineering is unlikely to remain a durable strategy, and claiming AI-generated code is worthless is unrealistic. Models primarily fail through ignorance of a codebase’s modules, standards, and risk assumptions, or through paranoia that adds unnecessary checks, fallbacks, and complexity. Engineers who understand the system can reject these choices, simplify them, and identify when the agent is confidently wrong. Technical communication is another lasting advantage because good writing is difficult to define, grade, and optimize, while newer models often produce recognizable “slop” or “Claudish” styles. The goal is to use AI while applying human context, judgment, and persuasion rather than becoming a meat proxy who forwards model output.

stories.title: Headroom-Drift Replay: A Primitive for Principled Replay Control in GRPO
stories.snippet: RL-based post-training for reasoning models is increasingly bottlenecked by repeated fresh rollout generation, particularly in agentic settings where environment interaction dominates wall-clock cost. Replay can reduce this burden by reusing past trajectories, but existing methods typically embed it within larger training pipelines involving exploration, experience restructuring, or mixed-policy optimization. This makes replay's own contribution difficult to isolate. We ask a focused question: how far can principled replay selection alone go? We introduce Headroom-Drift Replay, a group-level r
stories.summary: The paper introduces Headroom-Drift Replay, a group-level replay control primitive designed to address the computational bottleneck of repeated fresh rollout generation in GRPO-based RL post-training for reasoning models, especially in agentic settings where environment interaction dominates wall-clock cost. The method decomposes replay selection into two independent decisions: Headroom, which ranks stored groups by remaining learning value, and Drift, which gates them based on compatibility with the current policy. The fresh on-policy stream remains unchanged, and the approach adds no auxiliary generation or training machinery. Experiments span mathematical reasoning, multimodal reasoning, and Agentic Search benchmarks, where this single intervention outperforms naive replay and matches or exceeds broader replay methods on Avg Mean@32. In Agentic Search, where environment interaction drives cost, the method achieves comparable quality at materially lower wall-clock time, with the paper accepted at COLM 2026.

stories.title: Masked Autoregressive Speech Enhancement with Continuous Neural Audio Codec Representations
stories.snippet: Most previous work on speech enhancement (SE) based on masked generative modeling relied on discrete token representations of audio signals, obtained using neural audio codecs (NACs). However, a recent study has shown that continuous latent representations of NACs can be advantageous for SE in terms of speech quality and intelligibility. In particular, we investigate a set of different decoding policies, ceteris par
stories.summary: A paper by Yoto Fujita, Simon Leglaive, and Laurent Girin, presented at IWAENC in September 2026, introduces MARSE, a masked autoregressive method for speech enhancement that operates on continuous neural audio codec representations. Prior work on masked generative modeling for speech enhancement relied on discrete token representations from neural audio codecs, though a recent study suggested continuous latent representations could better preserve speech quality and intelligibility. MARSE performs iterative decoding of masked clean speech frames using these continuous codec representations. The authors compare several decoding policies while holding constant the DNN architecture (a Conformer model), the NAC (the DAC codec), and the training setup. Their results indicate that MARSE provides a flexible trade-off between enhancement performance and computational cost. Audio examples and code are made available online alongside the paper.

stories.title: Towards Numerical TOHTN Planning with SMT-based HTN-SAT Encoding
stories.snippet: While HTN planning has received significant attention in recent years, support for numerical reasoning remains very limited. In this paper, we investigate numerical Totally-Ordered HTN (TOHTN) planning and show how standard SAT-based encodings can be naturally extended with SMT to handle numeric fluents. In addition, we introduce a benchmark suite for numerical TOHTN planning, providing a first common basis for evaluation in this setting. Experimental results show that this simple encoding already constitutes a competitive baseline. This work opens the way to more expressive approaches to HTN
stories.summary: The paper investigates numerical reasoning in Totally-Ordered HTN (TOHTN) planning, an area that has received limited attention in HTN planning research. The authors extend standard SAT-based encodings with SMT to handle numeric fluents, showing that this combination naturally supports numerical reasoning in hierarchical planning. They also introduce a benchmark suite for numerical TOHTN planning, providing the first common basis for evaluation in this setting. Experimental results demonstrate that this straightforward encoding already constitutes a competitive baseline for the domain. Published at the 9th ICAPS Workshop on Hierarchical Planning (HPlan 2026), the work opens the way toward more expressive approaches to HTN planning that incorporate numerical constraints.

stories.title: RATL: Learning from Retrieved Residuals for Robust Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting
stories.snippet: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) complements parametric models with retrieved external evidence. The same idea is attractive for continuous-output regression, but directly reusing retrieved target values is often not robust when samples differ in output level, numerical scale, or local dynamics. Moreover, conventional forecasting pipelines generally use residuals for model optimization and error diagnosis, but do not retain individual historical residual examples as memory that can be accessed at inference time.For multivariate time-series forecasting, we propose RATL, a plug-in residual-r
stories.summary: RATL is a plug-in residual-retrieval and feedback-correction method proposed for multivariate time-series forecasting. Unlike retrieval-augmented approaches that directly reuse retrieved target values, RATL freezes a base forecaster to construct retrieval keys and converts that model's historical forecast residuals into a train-only memory. At inference, it retrieves residual trajectories from similar historical contexts under causal availability constraints and employs a set-aware router over forecast blocks and variables to select and combine those trajectories. Experiments using iTransformer as the primary frozen base forecaster against multiple strong baselines show that historical residuals matched to the current context contain reusable forecasting information, with RATL improving frozen base forecasters in most settings. Ablations further indicate that learned routing strengthens raw residual feedback, while validation-based correction-strength selection limits residual effects. Across real-world benchmarks, the approach transfers across backbones and shifts the retrieved object from historical target values to base-model-specific forecast errors.

stories.title: Sparse auto-regressive modeling for scene generation from multi-view images
stories.snippet: Generating complete 3D scenes from sparse, unconstrained views is a fundamental challenge in 3D vision which requires reasoning beyond observed content while remaining computationally tractable. Existing feed-forward reconstruction methods are inherently limited to content visible in the input images, while 3D generative modeling is hindered by the high computational cost of dense volumetric representations and the scarcity of large-scale 3D supervision. We introduce SPAR3S, a sparse voxel-aligned 3D latent generative model for conditional scene completion without requiring ground-truth 3D dat
stories.summary: SPAR3S is a sparse voxel-aligned 3D latent generative model designed for conditional scene completion from sparse, unconstrained views without requiring ground-truth 3D supervision. The method operates in a compact latent space where only occupied voxels are represented, learned directly from multi-view images through photometric supervision via differentiable 3D Gaussian Splatting. Given a partial set of observed voxels encoded from sparse input views, scene completion is framed as predicting the missing latent tokens and their spatial support within the voxel grid. A masked autoregressive transformer jointly models voxel occupancy and latent token values, enabling efficient and spatially consistent generation of unseen regions. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their method on synthetic indoor scenes, achieving higher novel-view quality than prior work, and further validate its generalization on the RealEstate10k dataset. The paper, authored by Thomas Lucas, Maxime Pietrantoni, Philippe Weinzaepfel, Wonjune Cho, Bardienus Pieter Duisterhof, Vincent Leroy, and Jerome Revaud, has been accepted at ECCV 2026.

stories.title: Audacity 4.0
stories.summary: Audacity 4.0.0 was released on September 3, marking a major update that rebuilds the application's interface on Qt with native high-DPI rendering. The release introduces a new clip-editing model where clips can be selected, grouped, moved freely between mono and stereo tracks, and split using a dedicated tool triggered by holding the S key. The interface offers customizable workspaces, light, dark, and high-contrast themes, and a new home screen with project previews, while legacy tool modes and Sync-Lock have been removed. Projects are now saved in the new .aup4 format, though .aup3 files can be opened and converted. Supported plugin formats include VST3, Nyquist, LV2 on Linux, and Audio Units on macOS, with official Windows builds adding ASIO support, though several Audacity 3 features such as Time Tracks, Note/MIDI tracks, and the Macro Manager are not yet available.

stories.title: .name Termination
stories.summary: Neil Fraser registered neil.fraser.name about twenty-five years ago, using it for his website, email, and API server, and also registered beverly.fraser.name for his daughter shortly after her birth. On 15 April 2026, Verisign proposed destroying the entire third level of the .name hierarchy to simplify administration, and ICANN approved the proposal on 28 July 2026. Although .name was originally run by Global Name Registry rather than Verisign, Verisign later acquired that company. Fraser discovered the change only when his registrar emailed him, meaning his website will vanish in February despite being paid until 2040, his email will disappear, and his IoT devices will stop working. If someone else registers the now-vacant fraser.name domain, they could hijack the email and hundreds of accounts associated with neil.fraser.name. Fraser is one of 22,000 people losing their domains under this decision.

stories.title: Audacity 4.0.0 Released
stories.summary: Audacity 4.0.0 has been released, representing a major rebuild of the application interface on Qt with native high-DPI rendering. The update introduces a new clip-editing model where clips can be selected directly by clicking their headers, with Shift-click enabling multi-clip selection for simultaneous editing, moving, trimming, and time stretching. Clips can now be grouped, moved freely between mono and stereo tracks, and overlapping clips replace rather than block each other. A dedicated splitting tool has been added, activated by pressing or holding the S key, along with commands for split-cut, split-delete, split-at-silences, and split-to-new-track operations. The interface now supports customizable toolbars and panels that can be docked, floated, or hidden, with layouts saveable as Workspaces including Modern, Classic, and Music presets. Light, dark, and high-contrast themes are also available, alongside improved paste handling, alignment guides, and per-project snap settings.

stories.title: jujutsu 0.45.0
stories.summary: The latest release of jj, version 0.45.0, introduces the new `jj converge` command that automatically resolves divergent commits by combining them, applying heuristics and falling back to user prompts when inconclusive. A notable breaking change is that `jj config {edit,set,unset} --user` now targets the first loaded user configuration file instead of prompting when multiple files exist, with a new `--file <PATH>` option available for targeting specific configuration files. Additionally, `jj git import` in non-colocated repositories no longer imports commits from a detached Git HEAD branch. The release also tracks Git HEAD state per worktree internally, preparing colocated repositories for support of multiple Git worktrees. Several bug fixes address issues including terminal corruption when pressing Ctrl+C in less, lost carriage returns in conflicted files, stale Git HEAD resets in colocated workspaces, and duplicate tree entries caused by external `git add` commands.
